title: Ki Tisa: Bezalel (Exodus 31:1–6)
hookLine: an artist filled "with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding"
tomorrow: Ki Tisa: even the sanctuary rests

cards: Who is the first person in the Torah that God says He has filled with the spirit of God? A prophet, maybe, or a king, or Moses himself. It's none of them.
Pharaoh once said the spirit of God was in Joseph, but these are God's own words, and they're about a craftsman: a man who works gold, silver and bronze, who cuts stones and carves wood.
For chapters, God has described the sanctuary: the ark, the lampstand, the curtains, the priest's clothes. Somebody has to actually make it. His name is Bezalel.

teach.h: FILLED WITH THE SPIRIT OF GOD.
teach.b: God says to Moses, see, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
And in the JPS 1917 translation: "I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship."
The Torah puts skilled hands on the same list as the spirit of God. His name helps.

Bezalel can be read as in the shadow of God, and the Talmud, in Berakhot, tells a story built on it. Moses gives Bezalel the instructions starting with the ark and the furniture, and only then the tent.
Bezalel answers: usually a person builds the house first and then brings the furniture in. Moses says: you must have been standing in the shadow of God, because that's exactly the order God told me.
The same page says Bezalel knew how to join the letters by which heaven and earth were made: a craftsman with the knowledge of creation in his fingers. And he isn't alone.
God gives him a partner, Oholiab, from the tribe of Dan.
Rashi notes that Dan was among the humblest tribes, and Judah among the greatest: the sanctuary was made by both together.

So a week of the sanctuary and its people ends: crushed olives for light, Moses stepping out of the frame, clothes that carry meaning, names on the heart, holy on the forehead, half a coin each, and now the artist with his hands full of spirit.

how: Bezalel's name is often invoked in Jewish life for art made in the service of holiness; the Bezalel school of art in Jerusalem, founded in 1906, is named after him.

games.q: you're Bezalel. Moses hands you the plans: first the ark and the furniture, then the tent. what do you say?
o: start building the ark right away.
ask: don't we build the house first, then bring the furniture in?
games.why: in the Talmud's story, Bezalel asks about the order, and Moses answers: you must have stood in the shadow of God, because that's what God told me.

practice: Make something small with your hands: fold a piece of paper into a shape, sketch the cup in front of you, tie a careful knot. Do it slowly and watch your fingers work, the small choices, the moment it comes out right.
If you pray, offer the work as it is; if not, just let your hands be fully here.

wordCard.voice: Ki Tisa. The portion where God names Bezalel, the craftsman filled with the spirit of God and the skill of his hands.

orig.note: Hebrew: Bezalel, which can be read as in the shadow of God.

carryVoice: Your line: craft is spirit. Skilled hands sit on the same list as wisdom. That's day three hundred sixty-four.
